exact_statement: For every fixed integer L>=0, let C_L retain each residual Fourier subset T with |T|<=L separately and merge all |T|>L into one tail. On a finite uniform Boolean cube define mu_i(T)=p_(T+i)/e_i, r_i(T)=p_T+p_(T+i), D_i^L=D(C_L mu_i||C_L r_i) and M^L=sum_i e_i[log2(1/e_i)-D_i^L], omitting irrelevant coordinates. For n>=max(6,2L+2), let f_n be the n-bit one-point defect, e=2^(1-n), m=2^floor(n/2), and G_n=f_n^tensor(m). Every Fourier coefficient of G_n is nonzero and every physical influence equals e, so I(G_n)=mn e tends to zero. Its genuine H/I<4 and M/I<=2, but M^L/I>=floor(n/2)-2-beta(n-1), beta=e sum_(j=0..L)binom(n-1,j), which diverges. The exact lost refund is M^L-M=sum_i e_i mu_i(tail)D(mu_i(.|tail)||r_i(.|tail)), and therefore its ratio is at least floor(n/2)-4-beta(n-1). No auxiliary parity or dummy coordinates are used. This refutes a universal payment using fixed low-degree atom inspection and one undifferentiated normalized tail, or weaker partitions, not the complete row KL, adaptive or structurally refined tail references, or FEI.
